_meta.purpose: Story Rank ladder for Mission Roulette solo story mode — draft.
rulesLocked: One life. You can only set spawn to a MEDBED ship/vehicle (medical ships; Ursa Medivac for ground) — respawn there = continue. With no medbed set you respawn at a station/city = game over. A medbed is your only safety net.
R0–R4 ships are RENTED; the Finisher is a PURCHASE — the ship you buy with earnings to graduate the track.

Rented ships only (until the Finisher). Rentals are forgiving: strip your weapons/gear and move them to your next rental and you keep them; you only lose a ship if you log off and back on past the rent. Re-renting is a chore, not a wipe (there's no cargo to lose unless you leave it aboard).
Frozen wallet: note your current aUEC; your story wallet starts at the run's amount (10k default, 0 for Beggar). Spend only what the run earns; existing money is off-limits.
Advance by DOING: clear each rank by completing a modest number of real missions of that rank's tier — works for maxed players, since the challenge is the constraints, not rep.
Length is emergent — a tense session or two, replayable — not a manufactured weeks-long grind.
_meta.r0: R0 Arrival is universal: everyone starts with 10k (0 for Beggar) and grabs a starter — Aurora ES / Mustang Alpha / Cutter — then does general jobs to afford their R1 ship.
_meta.medbedNote: ONLY a MEDBED lets you set spawn (medical ships + Ursa Medivac ground vehicle) — a normal bed does not. No medbed = no respawn = one death is final. Rentable medbeds: C8R Pisces Rescue, Cutlass Red, Apollo Triage/Medivac, Ursa Medivac (carried). This is WHY the Merc track is the medbed line; other tracks either run without a net (fragile early game — starters have no medbed) or carry an Ursa Medivac inside a vehicle-bay ship for a ground respawn.
_meta.shipCaveat: Rental ships are confirmed from the 4.8.2 wiki pull. Live game is 4.9 (4.10 soon) — re-verify. Finisher ships are PURCHASES (not rentals): Redeemer, 400i, Starlancer TAC (author-provided).

advancement.perRank: ~10 missions of the rank's tier (modest, tunable). R4's 'count' is the hero adventure itself.

aspirations.rule: Pick 1 main (required — drives the ladder + start hub) + up to 2 secondary (optional — blend into the beat pool).

path.outlaw: illegal-tab missions, crimestat, forced Pyro cool-off; opens Contested + Valakkar

pacifist.desc: No combat by your hand — industrial/social pool.

off-grid.desc: No station services (repair/refuel/rearm manual or player-assisted). Honor-scored badge; docking to re-rent is allowed.

beggar.desc: Displayed as 'Broke' (key stays 'beggar'). Start with no ship and no credits — earn your first ship on foot. May bum rides/help, never money. Starts at a no-rental location.

start.note: Funded starts use the track's startHub (randomized). Beggar starts are no-rental spots — hitch a ride to a hub.
start.pyro: Never a start — Pyro is a destination, not a spawn.

backstory.note: Assembled from SLOTS into 2 sentences: '{Origin}, you {identity} — {motivation}{sideline}. {CityClause}, {closer}.' Rolled once per story (run.backstory), rerollable on the briefing. Content stays generic SC (UEE/corp/colony/crimestat/'the black') — no real NPCs or events. {loc} = the rolled starting city (startLoc, city name only).
origin: ex-UEE Navy, wrong side of a bad discharge
a corp lifer who finally walked out
a second-gen spacer raised in a cockpit
fresh off a dead-end colony world
an old hand with more scars than credits
a drifter running a borrowed name
a hangar rat who taught yourself to fly

bounty: run down skips across the black
take the contracts steadier pilots pass on
make your living down a gun-sight
miner: read rock better than most read people
pull ore the big outfits overlook
know a good rock by the way it rings
hauler: move cargo nobody else will touch
know every back-route in the system
salvager: pick the bones of dead ships
make dead ships pay one panel at a time
explorer: map the black one jump at a time
chart what everyone else flies past
read the dark between the beacons
merc: fight for whoever signs the chit
take the jobs that need boots on the ground

motivation: one big job from walking away
just to keep the lights on
out to prove the washouts wrong
building toward a ship of your own
because it's the only life you know
saving for a berth somewhere quiet
still chasing the name you never made

lawful: and you keep it clean — mostly
with no crimestat to your name yet
lawful-beggar: empty pockets and a clean record
nothing to your name but a clean sheet
outlaw: already on the law's bad side
outlaw-beggar: broke, marked, and used to it
